messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a weird 429 pattern on canary for POST /v1/generate (per-route quotas). Clients get a 429, Retry-After: 3, then immediately a follow-up request within that window succeeds. Anyone seen a token-bucket reset race like this?

raj: hmm, can you paste the raw response headers + a minimal curl?

maria: yep, here's a snippet from the proxied response we logged: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:abc123
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Route-Quota-Window: 60
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"quota_exceeded","hint":"soft-quota","reset_at":"2026-03-17T12:34:56Z"}
```
Behavior: client retries after 1s (ignores Retry-After) and gets 200 with same model/route within that 3s window. Logs show a different backend machine served it.

simon: sounds like a distributed counter + lease expiry problem. If one host decremented and thought bucket was empty, then another host's local counter was stale and still had tokens. When the first host publishes the empty state, race wins sometimes.

elaine: do we have consistency guarantees for per-route quotas right now? I thought we had a best-effort sync (eventual) to keep tail latency down.

raj: correct — per-route quotas are sharded and asynchronous. We accept some transient over-accept to preserve p99 latency. But that means 429s are "soft" in practice. We should make that explicit in the contract so SDKs/clients can handle it.

maria: agreed — but product folks want strong guarantees for paid dedicated customers. We need a contract that preserves backward compatibility for existing clients while clearly signaling "soft 429" vs "hard 429".

simon: proposal: leave Retry-After as-is for backwards compat, and add an opt-in header that communicates the quota's enforcement mode and a monotonic bucket generation id. Something like: 
```
X-Redwood-Quota-Mode: soft|hard
X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket-Gen: 20260317123456-abc123
X-Redwood-Quota-Reset-Epoch: 1710700496  # unix sec when bucket resets
```
If clients see mode=soft they can choose to backoff gently instead of hard fail. Also the bucket-gen helps SDKs detect that a Retry-After window might still be inconsistent across nodes.

elaine: I like keeping Retry-After immutable. Adding X-Redwood-* keeps us from breaking third-party clients. Also suggest X-Redwood-Quota-LocalExpiryMs to show when the local node will stop serving cached tokens.

raj: SDK stuff: I'll add handling in the JS/Go SDK to prefer X-Redwood-Quota-Mode when present, and fall back to Retry-After if not present. Also will log bucket-gen mismatches. Ping me the trace id and I'll attach it to a unit test.

maria: trace id: rwd-20260317-canary-4721. Also filing an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4982 (draft description + logs).

raj: thx — I'll open a small PR to add header parsing + a minimal integration test that simulates two shards returning different states. Want to ship the header on canary first.

simon: server-side mitigation suggestion: for dedicated customers we should flip per-route quotas to strict global accounting (linearizable) or use a lease-based token allocator to avoid accept-after-429. For hosted tiers, keep eventual but clearly label mode=soft.

elaine: rollout plan:
- canary: add X-Redwood-* headers, no behavior change (just signals)
- collect telemetry for 48h (bucket-gen mismatch rate, accept-after-429 events)
- if mismatch > threshold, toggle stricter enforcement on a small set of routes or dedicated accounts
- announce to SDKs (minor version bump)

raj: timeline wise I can have the SDK change + tests by EOW if we land header on canary today. Can someone do the server-side PR to add the headers?

maria: I'll put up the server PR this afternoon (small middleware that appends the X-Redwood-* headers when quota check runs). Will mark it WIP and link the canary deployment.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: svc=quota-checker image=quoter:v2026-03-17-canary-3 cid=rwd-canary-4721

raj: once canary is up, I'll run a quick integration that replays the two-shard race and assert SDK logs a bucket-gen mismatch and uses X-Redwood-Quota-Mode to adjust backoff.

elaine: one more backwards-compat note — some clients treat any 429 as absolute and stop; others keep retrying aggressively. We should update the docs and add a short note in the API contract: "429 may be soft (best-effort) or hard (enforced). Prefer X-Redwood-Quota-Mode when present."

maria: will update the API contract doc PR after canary numbers come in. @raj please @me on the SDK PR for a quick review.

raj: will do. Thanks all — seems like a clear path.

maria: thanks! I’ll post telemetry in ~48h and follow up with numbers. :thumbsup:
